🎯 Objectives
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:
- Tell the difference between direct and reported (indirect) speech.
- Change tenses when reporting what someone said.
- Change pronouns and time expressions correctly.
- Report statements, questions and commands.

🔍 Warm-up
Direct: Sami said, "I am tired." Reported: Sami said that he was tired. Notice the changes: the quotation marks disappear, "I" becomes "he", and "am" becomes "was". This lesson explains those changes step by step.

I. Direct and reported speech
📘 Rule
- Direct speech = the exact words someone says, inside quotation marks. She said, "I like this book."
- Reported speech = we tell someone what was said, without quotation marks and usually with "that". She said that she liked that book.

📏 Form (basic pattern)
subject + said / told + (that) + reported sentence.
- "say" does not need a person after it: He said that ...
- "tell" needs a person after it: He told me that ...

✏️ Worked examples
- Direct: "I am happy." → Reported: He said that he was happy.
- Direct: "We live in Tunis." → Reported: They said that they lived in Tunis.

II. Backshift: changing the tense
📘 Rule (the key point)
When the reporting verb is in the PAST (said, told), the tense usually moves ONE step back into the past. This is called backshift.
📏 Tense changes
- present simple → past simple: "I work" → he said he worked.
- present continuous → past continuous: "I am working" → he said he was working.
- past simple → past perfect: "I worked" → he said he had worked.
- present perfect → past perfect: "I have worked" → he said he had worked.
- will → would: "I will help" → he said he would help.
- can → could: "I can swim" → he said he could swim.

✏️ Worked examples
- "I feel tired." → She said that she felt tired.
- "We are studying." → They said that they were studying.
- "I have finished." → He said that he had finished.
- "I will call you." → She said that she would call me.

🛠️ Method: reporting a statement
Step 1 — Remove the quotation marks and add "that" (optional).
Step 2 — Change the pronouns to fit the new speaker.
Step 3 — Move the tense one step back (backshift).
Step 4 — Change time and place words if needed.

III. Changing pronouns, time and place
📘 Rule (pronouns)
Pronouns change to match the point of view of the person reporting.
- "I" → he / she; "we" → they; "you" → I / he / she; "my" → his / her.
✏️ Worked example
- Direct: Leila said, "I love my city." → Reported: Leila said that she loved her city.

📘 Rule (time and place expressions)
Because we report later, time and place words often change:
- now → then
- today → that day
- tomorrow → the next day / the following day
- yesterday → the day before
- here → there
- this → that
✏️ Worked examples
- "I will travel tomorrow." → He said he would travel the next day.
- "I am busy today." → She said she was busy that day.

IV. Reporting questions and commands
📘 Rule (questions)
When we report a question, we use normal word order (subject + verb), NOT question order, and we do not use "?".
- Yes/No questions: use "if" or "whether".
- Wh- questions: keep the question word.
📏 Form
- Direct: "Do you speak English?" → Reported: She asked if I spoke English.
- Direct: "Where do you live?" → Reported: He asked where I lived.

✏️ Worked examples
- "Are you ready?" → She asked whether I was ready.
- "What time is it?" → He asked what time it was.

📘 Rule (commands and requests)
To report an order or a request, use "tell / ask + person + to + base verb".
- Direct: "Close the door." → Reported: She told me to close the door.
- Direct: "Please help me." → Reported: He asked me to help him.
- Negative command: "Don't be late." → She told me not to be late.

👀 Note
When the reporting verb is in the PRESENT (says, tells), there is NO backshift.
- He says, "I am tired." → He says that he is tired.

✏️ Worked paragraph
Yesterday my friend Amine called me. He said that he was preparing for the English exam and that he had studied all week. He asked me if I wanted to revise together. Then he told me to bring my notes and not to forget my dictionary. I said that I would come the next day.

⚠️ Common mistakes
1. Forgetting backshift: He said he is tired → He said he was tired.
2. Keeping question word order: She asked where do I live → She asked where I lived.
3. Using "?" in reported questions.
4. Not changing pronouns: Leila said that I loved my city (when reporting about Leila) → she loved her city.
5. Using "say" with a person: He said me → He told me / He said to me.

⭐ Recap
- Reported speech tells what someone said, without quotation marks.
- With a past reporting verb, the tense shifts one step back (backshift).
- Change pronouns, and change time/place words (tomorrow → the next day).
- Report questions with "if / whether" or the wh-word and normal word order.
- Report commands with "tell / ask + person + (not) to + base verb".

📘 Language bank
Reporting verbs: say, said, tell, told, ask, asked, explain, answer.
Tense shifts: is → was, are → were, do → did, have → had, will → would, can → could.
Time shifts: now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before.
Useful sentences: He said that he was tired. / She asked if I was ready. / He asked where I lived. / She told me to close the door. / He told me not to be late.

📝 Practice
Exercise 1 — Change into reported speech.
1. Sami said, "I am tired."
2. Leila said, "I have finished my homework."
3. They said, "We will travel tomorrow."
4. He said, "I can swim very well."

Exercise 2 — Report these questions.
1. She asked, "Do you speak English?"
2. He asked, "Where do you live?"
3. The teacher asked, "Are you ready?"

Exercise 3 — Report these commands.
1. "Close the door," she said.
2. "Please help me," he said.
3. "Don't be late," the teacher said.

✅ Answers
Exercise 1: 1. Sami said that he was tired. 2. Leila said that she had finished her homework. 3. They said that they would travel the next day. 4. He said that he could swim very well.
Exercise 2: 1. She asked if I spoke English. 2. He asked where I lived. 3. The teacher asked whether I was ready.
Exercise 3: 1. She told me to close the door. 2. He asked me to help him. 3. The teacher told me not to be late.

🗣️ Speaking task
Play "message passing". Student A whispers a sentence to Student B ("I love football"). Student B reports it to the class: "A said that he/she loved football." Check the backshift together.

👀 Extra note
Three changes happen when you report a past statement:
1. Tense shifts back one step (am → was, will → would, have → had).
2. Pronouns change to fit the new speaker (I → he/she).
3. Time and place words change (tomorrow → the next day, here → there).
For questions, use normal word order and "if/whether" or the wh-word; for commands, use "tell/ask + person + (not) to + verb".

📋 Summary
- Direct speech = exact words in quotation marks; reported speech = no quotation marks, usually with "that".
- Backshift: when the reporting verb is in the past (said/told), the tense moves one step back.
- Tense shifts: present simple → past simple, present continuous → past continuous, present perfect → past perfect, will → would, can → could.
- No backshift when the reporting verb is in the present (He says that he is tired).
- Pronouns change to match the new speaker: I → he/she, we → they, my → his/her.
- Time and place words shift: now → then, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, yesterday → the day before, here → there.
- Reported questions use normal word order (no "?"): yes/no questions with if/whether, wh-questions keep the question word.
- Reported commands: tell/ask + person + (not) + to + base verb (She told me to close the door).
- "say" never takes a person directly (say to / tell + person); "tell" always needs a person.
